text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Abdullah's talks in Beirut will cover joint projects. Prince becomes first senior Saudi official to visit Lebanon in nearly two decades when he arrives on Thursday.
- Cabinet earmarks 150 billion Lebanese pounds for development of rural regions.
- Head of lawyers' syndicate says Lebanon is in crisis on all fronts including general freedoms.
- Former Lebanese President Gemayel calls on Washington to flex muscles to push Syria into leaving Lebanon.
- Israel shells areas in southern Lebanon.
- Legal telephone tapping has stopped pending further reviews of system, says head of committee charged with studying issue.
- Parliamentary committees call on government to retreat from decision to raise customs fees on imported cars.

- Syria, Hizbollah and a Shi'ite council adopt similar positions against hunger strike; former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili is urging residents of Bekaa Valley to start hunger strike and civil disobedience campaign on July 4 to pressure Beirut government into easing poverty in area.
- Islamic resistance attacks Israeli positions in southern Lebanon.
